newsitem.title: CANADA: East Manitoba saw some frost, Prairies to be sunny.
newsitem.headline: East Manitoba saw some frost, Prairies to be sunny.

text.p: Parts of Manitoba's grain belt east of Winnipeg Friday morning saw some frost while the Prairies were forecast to see mainly sunny skies and warm temperatures, Environment Canada said.
"It looks like there were a few touches of frost east of Winnipeg," meteorologist Gerald Machnee told Reuters.
Sprague, two miles north of Minnesota, saw an overnight low of 0.6 Celsius at chest level with partly cloudy skies and winds of three knots, Machnee said.
Ground level temperatures can be 2.0 to 5.0 Celsius below chest level temperatures on sky, wind and moisture conditions.
Gretna, two miles north of North Dakota, saw an overnight low of 1.1 Celsius, Machnee said.
Winnipeg saw an overnight low of 3.0 Celsius.
The rest of the Prairies were 6.0 Celsius or warmer overnight except Hudson Bay, Saskatchewan, which saw a low of 4.0 Celsius, he said.
Alberta should see sunny skies and highs of 22 to 29 Celsius.
Saskatchewan should see mainly sunny skies with highs of 22 to 25 Celsius.
Manitoba should see sunny skies and highs of 15 to 20 Celsius.
